name: Somsri Lumsam
profile: Listed by Hurun Global (2018-2024) at ~US$1.2bn with CP Group as source of wealth. Searches found no person of this exact spelling linked to CP Group (owned by the Chearavanont family); a 'Somsri Lamsam' appears on a 2023 Thai rich list without a stated business link.
notes: Identity unresolved: the name is likely a romanisation of Somsri Lamsam (Lamsam family is associated with Kasikornbank/Muang Thai, not CP Group), so the Hurun CP Group attribution may be an error. Verify in Thai-language sources before any outreach. Caproasia 2023 list: https://www.caproasia.com/2023/04/15/2023-top-20-richest-in-thailand/

name: Jeremy Allaire
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Circle Internet Group (NYSE: CRCL)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Allaire Corp. (ColdFusion; IPO 1999, sold to Macromedia) and Brightcove (online video, IPO 2012). Pivoted to crypto in 2013 co-founding Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, and took it public in June 2025, the first IPO of a stablecoin issuer.
interesting_fact: He has now taken three companies public: Allaire Corp. (1999), Brightcove (2012) and Circle (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In 1994-96, fresh out of Macalester College (political science and philosophy), he worked with Noam Chomsky and his wife Carol to build the first comprehensive online archive of Chomsky's political writings.
notes: Very public and active on X (@jerallaire); regular podcast/conference guest on stablecoins and payments. Circle press office is the best route.

name: Arvind Nithrakashyap
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Rubrik, Inc. (NYSE: RBRK)
profile: IIT Madras (1995) and UMass Amherst (MS 1997) computer scientist who spent years at Oracle, where he co-founded the Exadata database platform, then led real-time ad infrastructure at Rocket Fuel. In 2013/14 he co-founded data-security company Rubrik, which IPO'd in 2024; his stake makes him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: At Oracle he co-founded Exadata, now one of Oracle's flagship database/storage platforms, before leaving to co-found Rubrik.
deep_cut_fact: At Rocket Fuel he architected the real-time bidding engine, leading ~30 engineers on an ad platform handling 50 billion requests a day at 50-60 ms latency; IIT Madras later gave him its Distinguished Alumnus Award.
notes: Low-profile technical founder but does keynotes/panels; route via Rubrik PR (Meghan Fintland, Head of Global PR, listed on releases).

name: Xiong Haitao
current_role: Actual controller of Gaojin Technology Industry Group (largest shareholder of Dongcai Technology, Gaomeng New Materials, Yichang Technology); vice chair of Dongcai Technology
profile: Chinese businesswoman, formerly a Kingfa Sci. & Tech. director (1998-May 2024) and ex-wife of Kingfa founder Yuan Zhimin; still a Kingfa shareholder (~1.5%). Through Gaojin Group she controls three Shanghai/Shenzhen-listed materials companies.
interesting_fact: Via Gaojin Technology Industry Group she is the ultimate controller of three separate A-share companies: Dongcai Technology (insulation/film materials), Gaomeng New Materials (adhesives) and Yichang Technology.
notes: Sensitive: in Jan 2026 the three listed companies announced she had been placed under detention (liuzhi) and investigation by the Sichuan Supervisory Commission; she resigned from Yichang's board 26 Jan 2026. Not a suitable outreach target at present. Source: https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202601273632524882.html

name: Wee Wei Ling
current_role: Executive Director (Sustainability Partnerships, Lifestyle & Asset), Pan Pacific Hotels Group; director, Kheng Leong and the Wee Foundation
profile: Eldest child of the late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw. At UOL's Pan Pacific Hotels Group she oversees owned hotels, the St. Gregory spa and Si Chuan Dou Hua restaurant brands and the group's sustainability and community partnerships; she also sits on the family's Kheng Leong property firm and Wee Foundation boards.
interesting_fact: A champion of inclusive hiring, she has pushed companies to treat employing people with special needs as corporate strategy rather than charity, and chaired Project We Care, the People's Association's CEO network for corporate volunteerism, from 2011.
deep_cut_fact: She personally curated Pan Pacific's corporate art collection of local artists, published as the book 'Along the Journey', and co-founded the performing-arts charity Extra.Ordinary People with her cousin Wee Boo Kuan; she kept a Delia Prvacki ceramic bought in 1997 even after selling the hotel it was in.
notes: Gives lifestyle-press interviews (Peak, Prestige, Tatler, Sleeper) on sustainability and inclusive hiring; best route is Pan Pacific Hotels Group corporate communications (Singapore) via its Mynewsdesk newsroom.

name: Baron Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza
profile: Swiss-based industrialist and art collector (Thyssen steel/industrial fortune), whose collection became Madrid's Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum. Died 27 April 2002 in Sant Feliu de Guíxols, Spain, aged 81.
interesting_fact: In 1993 Spain acquired the bulk of his art collection, now displayed at the Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
notes: Deceased (2002). Name in input is misspelled 'Bornesmisza'. Only listed on Forbes 1996.

name: Pedro Brescia Moreyra
current_role: Co-Chairman, Grupo Breca (Peru); Vice Chairman, Rímac Seguros
profile: Third-generation member (born 1971, son of Mario Brescia Cafferata) of the family behind Breca, Peru's largest conglomerate (Minsur tin/copper mining, TASA fishmeal, Rímac insurance, BBVA Perú stake, Melón cement, real estate). Formerly Breca's general manager, he now co-chairs the group with cousin Alex Fort Brescia and sits on many group boards.
interesting_fact: Breca's mining arm Minsur is one of the world's largest tin producers and, through Marcobre, runs the Mina Justa copper project; Pedro sits on both boards.
deep_cut_fact: A Universidad de Lima business graduate with a Kellogg MBA, he serves on the board of Aporta (Breca's social-impact platform) and is a director of the Instituto Peruano de Economía think tank.
notes: Do not confuse with his uncle Pedro Brescia Cafferata (1921-2014). Family is very private; route via Breca corporate communications. Energy/mining angle (Minsur, Marcobre) fits the podcast.

name: Binny Bansal
current_role: Founder, OppDoor (Singapore) and co-founder/chairman, xto10x Technologies; invests via Three State Ventures
profile: IIT Delhi computer-science graduate from Chandigarh who co-founded Flipkart with Sachin Bansal in 2007 after a stint at Amazon, later serving as Flipkart CEO and group CEO before leaving in 2018. Now Singapore-based, he backs startups and runs OppDoor, a platform helping e-commerce brands expand into new markets.
interesting_fact: Before Flipkart he and Sachin Bansal first considered building a comparison-shopping search engine, but judged India's e-commerce market too small and started an online bookstore instead.
deep_cut_fact: Google rejected him twice before he joined Amazon as a software engineer in 2007; earlier he spent about 18 months at Sarnoff Corporation after IIT Delhi.
notes: Input spelling 'Bansaal' is a typo. Lives in Singapore; best route is LinkedIn or via OppDoor/xto10x. Avoid referencing his 2018 Flipkart exit.

name: George Feldstein
profile: Founder and chairman of Crestron Electronics, the AV and building-automation control company he started in 1969 in a room above a deli in New Jersey. Died 4 November 2014 (some sources say 5 Nov), aged 73; Crestron remains family-owned.
interesting_fact: He received both InfoComm's Adele de Berri Lifetime Achievement Award and CEDIA's Lifetime Achievement Award.
notes: Deceased (Nov 2014). Crestron is now run by his family; contact Crestron corporate communications if relevant.

name: Harshil Mathur
profile: IIT Roorkee graduate who co-founded Razorpay with batchmate Shashank Kumar in 2014 (Y Combinator-backed), building India's largest payment gateway by volume. Razorpay, valued at $7.5bn, now spans payments, banking, payroll and POS and is preparing for an Indian IPO.
interesting_fact: He has said nearly 100 banks rejected Razorpay before one agreed to partner, an early hurdle he credits with shaping the company.
deep_cut_fact: Razorpay began in 2014 as a social crowdfunding project 'to enable people to fund and help others in distress'; struggling to integrate payments, he and Kumar pivoted to payments. Before that he was a wireline field engineer at Schlumberger.
notes: Media-friendly and active on X/podcasts. Razorpay newsroom contact page (dated ~2021) also names individual comms staff.

name: Huang Yi
current_role: Chairman and executive director, Zhongsheng Group Holdings (HKEX: 0881)
profile: Co-founded Zhongsheng Group with CEO Li Guoqiang in 1998 and built it into one of China's largest car-dealer networks, focused on luxury and mid-to-high-end brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Lexus, Porsche and Land Rover. He sets group strategy as chairman of the Hong Kong-listed company.
interesting_fact: Zhongsheng is one of China's largest national car dealerships, centred on luxury marques like Mercedes-Benz, Lexus and Porsche.
deep_cut_fact: After a 1983 economics degree from Xiamen University he spent 1984-94 at state-owned China Resources Machinery, importing cars and machinery, and was named an 'economist' by the trade ministry in 1990; in 1994 he joined Hong Kong's Huaji Auto and became a shareholder in 1996.
notes: Low public profile. Route via Zhongsheng investor relations (company site was unreachable from this environment, so no IR email verified). Not to be confused with Yunnan politician Huang Yi.

name: Rajat Agrawal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Gravita India Ltd (Jaipur)
profile: First-generation entrepreneur who founded Gravita in Jaipur in 1992; it grew into one of India's largest lead recyclers, also recycling aluminium, plastics and copper, with plants in India, Africa and Sri Lanka and customers in ~38 countries. Listed on Indian exchanges, the company has become a recycling and circular-economy growth story.
interesting_fact: Gravita began in 1992 as a welding and surface-coating company before Agrawal spotted the global opportunity in lead recycling; it now runs recycling plants across India, Africa and Sri Lanka.
notes: Recycling/battery-materials angle fits energy theme. Early-career details (MNIT engineering, L&T stockist, family home lost) appear only on low-quality aggregator sites, so they were not used. info@ is the company's general address.

name: Jose And Jaime Said
profile: Forbes 1999 joint listing for Chile's Said family (Parque Arauco malls, Embotelladora Andina Coca-Cola bottling, BHIF/BBVA Chile, later Scotiabank Chile stake, Edelpa). Patriarch José Said Saffie, founder of Grupo Said and chairman of Parque Arauco and Scotiabank Chile, died 23 July 2020 in Santiago aged 90.
interesting_fact: José Said Saffie, born in Arequipa, Peru, brought Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya into Chile's BHIF bank, which became BBVA Chile.
notes: José Said Saffie is deceased (2020; source https://www.emol.com/noticias/Economia/2020/07/23/992820/Fallece-Jose-Said-empresario.html). 'Jaime' is ambiguous: Jaime Said Handal (a cousin-branch Andina shareholder) vs. other Jaime Saids; could not confirm which or his status. Family wealth now held by José's heirs (Inversiones Cabildo) and the Said Handal branch.

name: Nurzhan Subkhanberdin
current_role: Private investor; former founder and chairman of Kazkommertsbank (exited 2015)
profile: Almaty-born (1964) banker who graduated in political economy from Moscow State University in 1988 and founded Kazkommertsbank, for years one of Kazakhstan's largest banks. He sold his stake and left the board in 2015 and has since kept a low profile, with investment interests including Hong Kong-based Meridian Capital.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he and six other Kazakh businessmen put about $100m into opening Haileybury Almaty, the first British private school in Central Asia.
notes: Very private; no published contact found. Wikipedia covers controversies (political-influence commentary, Paradise Papers reporting on Meridian) which should be avoided in outreach. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nurzhan_Subkhanberdin

name: Sergio Jesús Mazón Rubio
current_role: Board member (since ~2005), Megacable Holdings; chairman, Mazón Corporativo, Ocean Garden Products and Dynatek de México (per financial-data profiles)
profile: Sonoran businessman and long-time Megacable Holdings director; Megacable, now one of Mexico's largest cable/broadband operators, began in 1978 when a group of Sonora and Sinaloa businessmen formed regional cable companies. He also chairs the family's Mazón Corporativo and San Diego-based seafood trader Ocean Garden Products. Educated at Tec de Monterrey and the University of Arizona.
interesting_fact: Megacable traces its origin to 1978, when a group of Mexican businessmen founded Visión por Cable de Sonora (VICASON) and Visión por Cable de Sinaloa.
notes: Very low profile; biography mainly from MarketScreener profiles (https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/SERGIO-JESUS-MAZON-RUBIO-A10IWH/experience/). He is not named on Megacable's current management page; no death report found, so alive status unconfirmed. Relationship to Enrique Mazón Rubio (long-time Naranjeros de Hermosillo baseball club president) unverified.

name: Bernhard Schadeberg
current_role: Co-owner and Managing Director, Krombacher Brauerei Bernhard Schadeberg GmbH & Co. KG
profile: Born 1965 in Kreuztal, he studied business administration, joined the family brewery in 1993 and took over as managing director from his father Friedrich Schadeberg in 2001. With his sister Petra Schadeberg-Herrmann he runs Krombacher, one of Germany's best-selling beer brands, whose group also includes Schweppes Germany and other drinks businesses.
interesting_fact: The brewery carries his grandfather's name: Bernhard Schadeberg senior took over management of the Krombach brewery in October 1922, and it has been family-run ever since.
deep_cut_fact: He went to school at the local Gymnasium in Kreuztal, a few kilometres from the brewery in Krombach, and in a 2008 FAZ interview reflected on how young people's drinking habits had changed ('Frueher haben junge Leute vier Tage durchgetrunken').
notes: Rarely gives interviews; route via Krombacher press office. Biography source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernhard_Schadeberg

name: Zhao Lin
current_role: Chairman, CEO and executive director, Nayuki Holdings (HKEX: 2150)
profile: Restaurant-industry veteran who co-founded premium tea-drinks chain Nayuki (Nai Xue de Cha) in Shenzhen in 2014 with his wife Peng Xin, whose online nickname 'Nai Xue' gave the brand its name. Nayuki listed in Hong Kong in 2021; he now chairs and runs the company as it shifts to smaller-format stores.
interesting_fact: The brand name comes from co-founder Peng Xin's online handle 'Nai Xue'; the couple registered the trademark in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2014 he and Peng Xin each put up 50,000 yuan to register Shenzhen Pindao Catering Management, Nayuki's original operating company, and pledged personal assets to borrow 8 million yuan for the first stores.
notes: Shares Hurun listing with wife Peng Xin. Route via Nayuki investor relations (IR site ir.naixue.com); no IR email verified.

name: Deborah A. Dolan-Sweeney
current_role: Director, Dolan Family Foundation and Dolan Children's Foundation; Dolan family shareholder in MSG Sports, MSG Entertainment and Sphere Entertainment
profile: Daughter of the late cable pioneer and HBO founder Charles F. Dolan (died 2024). A former Cablevision Systems director (to 2016), she holds a share of the Dolan family stakes in the Madison Square Garden companies and AMC Networks and is involved in the family's philanthropic foundations.
interesting_fact: Her father Charles Dolan founded HBO and Cablevision; by the late 1990s the family owned the New York Knicks, New York Rangers, Madison Square Garden and Radio City Music Hall.
notes: Very private family member with no public-facing role; roles mainly from MarketScreener (https://ca.marketscreener.com/insider/DEBORAH-DOLAN-SWEENEY-A01AU8/experience/). Cablevision board dates vary by source (2008 or 2011 start). Avoid confusing with Kristin Dolan (sister-in-law, ex-AMC Networks CEO).

name: Yasemin Zeynep Keyman
current_role: Shareholder, ENKA İnşaat ve Sanayi (per Forbes)
profile: Listed by Forbes as one of more than a dozen family members holding shares in ENKA, Turkey's leading private power producer and a major global contractor, founded in 1957 by Şarık Tara and his brother-in-law Sadi Gülçelik. No independent public information about her role or family branch was found.
interesting_fact: ENKA's name comes from the first syllables of the Turkish words 'enişte' and 'kayınbirader', both meaning brother-in-law, honouring its two co-founders.
notes: Not a public figure; family branch unverified. ENKA (power plants, construction of US embassies) fits the energy angle, but outreach should go to ENKA corporate/IR or to chairman Sinan Tara. enka@enka.com is the company's general address.

name: Zhu Tao
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Scientific Officer and Executive Director, CanSino Biologics (HKEX: 6185; SSE: 688185)
profile: Vaccine scientist (PhD chemical engineering, University of Pittsburgh 2003; postdoc at Carnegie Mellon) who co-founded Tianjin-based CanSino Biologics in 2009 after working in Canada (reportedly at Sanofi Pasteur). He leads its R&D, which produced the Convidecia COVID-19 vaccines; his wealth peaked with CanSino's 2020-21 share surge.
interesting_fact: He led development of Convidecia Air, described as the world's first inhaled COVID-19 vaccine, and Convidecia, the WHO-recommended adenovirus-vector COVID-19 vaccine.
deep_cut_fact: Before COVID-19, he led development of China's only available recombinant Ebola vaccine and the country's first tetravalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine; he built five platform technologies, from viral vectors to mRNA, and holds 29 patents.
notes: Also listed as a PI at Nankai University's State Key Laboratory of Medicinal Chemical Biology. Route via CanSino IR. Sanofi Pasteur role is from press reporting (https://www.tbsnews.net/node/108580).
